prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures a top-down view from the camera wearer standing or sitting immediately behind and above a child seated at a white desk, with curtains and a wall in the background roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres away and dark floor space to the right at 1.5 to 2.0 metres. The child's head at the lower right (about 0.3 to 0.4 metres from the camera wearer) and the camera wearer's own left arm, knee, or held smartphone at the bottom left/centre (0.2 to 0.5 metres) appear brightest, while the desk surface sits at a uniform mid-grey around 0.6 to 0.8 metres with a desk lamp on the far left edge (~0.8 metres). The child faces downward and slightly left toward an open workbook on the desk, never looking toward the camera wearer, and everything on the desk—the workbook, pen, cable grommet, and lamp—is within arm's reach of both the child and the camera wearer. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's left hand moves from hovering above the child's head in frame 1 to touching the back of the child's neck in frame 2, then retreats out of view as a bright smartphone appears at the bottom centre in frames 3 and 4 (~0.3 metres away, partially occluding the child's left forearm), before the camera wearer's raised left forearm re-enters on the left in frame 5 while the child's left hand moves up to touch her own left ear. The map clarifies the continuous vertical distance separation between the elevated foreground limbs/head and the flat desk plane below that is foreshortened in RGB, though it is unreliable on flat or thin surface items—completely losing the open workbook, the pen tip in early frames, and the phone's screen bevels, while blurring the raised arm in frame 5 into the desk's depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground bodies and a few desk objects against an unlabelled black background, separating the child at the lower right (0.3 to 0.6 metres from the camera wearer) from the camera wearer's own limbs on the left and bottom (0.2 to 0.5 metres) and the desk lamp at the upper left (~0.8 metres away and ~0.5 metres left of the child). The child's head and torso are oriented forward and downward toward the desk surface away from the camera wearer's gaze, while the lower bodies of both individuals remain largely out of view below the bottom frame edge. Across the sequence, the masks track the camera wearer's left arm reaching across the child's left arm in frames 1 and 2 (partially occluding the workbook and the child's sleeve), retreating in frames 3 and 4 as a 'cell phone' mask appears at the bottom centre (~0.3 metres from the camera) alongside the camera wearer's knee on the bottom left, and re-entering as a raised forearm on the left in frame 5 while the child's left arm shifts right to her head. While the map cleanly delineates the boundary of the smartphone and separates the overlapping arms of the two people in frame 1, it is highly unreliable in class labelling and completeness: it misclassifies the desk lamp as a 'toothbrush' in frames 1–2 and 'scissors' in frames 3–5, merges the camera wearer's arm and the child's left arm into a single 'person' mask in frame 2, and erroneously labels almost the entire white desk surface as a 'person' in frame 5 while missing the workbook and pen entirely.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D skeletal keypoints (yellow) and dense hand meshes (magenta) for the visible upper extremities within 0.3 to 0.7 metres of the camera wearer, leaving the background room and desk completely black. Across frames 1 to 4, a cluster of disconnected yellow facial/head keypoints on the right marks the child's head facing downward and slightly left toward the desk (away from the camera wearer), positioned roughly 0.15 to 0.25 metres to the right of her left hand resting on the workbook. In frame 1, only the camera wearer's elevated left hand is tracked just left of the child's head; in frame 2, both the child's left hand on the desk and the camera wearer's left hand at the back of the child's neck are tracked along with a tangled yellow arm skeleton connecting them across the lower left. In frames 3 and 4, only the child's left hand resting on the workbook (~0.6 metres from the camera wearer, within arm's reach of both people) and her head keypoints are detected, and in frame 5 the tracked hand and forearm skeleton shift ~0.2 metres rightward and upward to the side of the child's head as her hand touches her ear. This map makes the fine finger articulation and palm orientation of the hands on the desk and near the head explicit in a way that can blend into skin tones in RGB, but it is very unreliable overall—completely missing the child's right hand holding the pen in every frame, missing the camera wearer's raised arm in frame 5, failing to form a coherent torso skeleton from the steep top-down angle, and falsely linking keypoints between the two different people in frame 2.
